declared.title: A mega-analysis of memory reports from eight peer-reviewed false memory implantation studies
declared.foundIn: the coordinator's brief (« Scoboria et al. 2017 mega-analysis », Memory); OpenAlex search of its title (2026-11-23)

population: 423 students (mean age 20.7) from 8 implantation studies in Canada, New Zealand, the US and the UK, told of a childhood event that never happened

findings.text: Coded with one common scheme, 30.4% of cases counted as false memories, partial ones included, and another 23% accepted the event to some degree

support.sentence: Using this scheme, 30.4% of cases were classified as false memories and another 23% were classified as having accepted the event to some degree.

findings.text: About 1 in 5 had a full or robust false memory (10.8% full, 11.1% robust); 8.5% had only a partial one

support.sentence: When we categorized the 423 memory reports according to the scheme described above (see Figure 1), 11.1% of the sample met the criteria for Robust memory, 10.8% met the criteria for Full memory, and 8.5% met the criteria for partial false memory, resulting in a combined false memory rate of 30.5%.
support.readBy: memory-rewritten reviser, 2026-11-26: accepted manuscript (WRAP 83729), Results, False memory formation across studies

findings.text: With self-relevant details and an imagination exercise (and no photo), the rate reached about 46%

support.sentence: When the suggestion included self-relevant information, an imagination procedure, and was not accompanied by a photo depicting the event, the memory formation rate was 46.1%.

limits: a mega-analysis (individual reports recoded), not a classic meta-analysis: 8 of 12 published studies (transcripts of 4 were lost), several by its own authors
« false memory » is the coders' judgement of transcripts, partial ones included; full + robust (about 22%) match the « full » memories of earlier studies
the 46.1% rests on 3 studies and 89 people (against 26.3% in the other conditions, full text)
the pooled studies include some negative events; this episode keeps to harmless everyday events
university students in four Western countries; no sample from the Middle East or North Africa
